answer: Each identity must seal a unique piece of data and periodically prove it still holds a distinct copy, so one operator with a thousand identities must store a thousand genuinely different sealed sectors rather than pointing the same cheap disk at a thousand names. Each head pays its own cost, paid in full, since the cost is per identity. The ember is the sealed sector, the falcon the replication challenge that proves it is still unique, and the wander the identity the sealed data is bound to; cloning the ember fails the falcon, and one sector cannot satisfy two wander bindings.
